question.en: Liquefied petroleum gas used in households is stored in steel tanks, with a valve switch on top of the tank. The pressure inside the tank is greater than atmospheric pressure. Leakage of petroleum gas can easily lead to poisoning, explosion, and fire accidents. It is known that the heat value of petroleum gas is 3.5×10^7 J/kg. When boiling water, assume that only 60% of the heat released by burning petroleum gas is absorbed by the water. Question: To heat [X] kg of water from an initial temperature of 20℃ to 100℃, how many grams of liquefied petroleum gas need to be completely burned? (Supplementary information: the specific heat capacity of water is 4.2×10^3 J/(kg·℃);) The volume of the water is 5 L. If we already know the answer to the above question is 80 g, what should the value of [X] in the question be?

en: [ temperature increase of water]=[ final temperature]-[ initial temperature]
[ heat released by fuel combustion] = [ mass of fuel consumed]*[ calorific value of liquefied petroleum gas]
[ heat absorbed by water] = [ efficiency]*[ heat released by fuel combustion]
[ mass of water] = [ heat absorbed by water]/([ temperature increase of water]*[specific heat capacity of water])

arguments.en_name: calorific value of liquefied petroleum gas

question.en:
During the May Day holiday, Dad drove Xiaohui from Hefei City along the Hechaowu Expressway to Wuhu Fantawild for a visit. When the car travels at a constant speed of 108 km/h on a straight road, the resistance force on the car is 1000 N, the engine efficiency is 30%, and the calorific value of the gasoline is 4.6×10^7 J/kg (assuming the gasoline is completely burned). Find:
If the car travels in this manner, what is the total work done by the traction force for the round trip of [X]? How much gasoline should Xiaohui remind Dad to add at least in kg? The final temperature of the water parameter is 100 ℃. If we already know the answer to the above question is 21.7 kg, what should the content corresponding to [X] in the question be?

en: [ heat released by complete combustion of gasoline] = [ calorific value of gasoline]*[ mass of gasoline]
[ work done by traction] = [ engine efficiency]*[ heat released by complete combustion of gasoline]
[ distance traveled] = [ work done by traction]/[resistance]

arguments.en_name: heat released by complete combustion of gasoline

question.en:
To ensure the safety of drinking water for all teachers and students, the school has installed a modern high-efficiency energy-saving boiler with a thermal efficiency of 80%, which can provide [X] boiling water daily. It is known that the specific heat capacity of water is 4.2×10^3 J/(kg•℃), and the calorific value of high-quality coal is 3.0×10^7 J/kg. Calculate:  
How much heat, in joules, is required to raise the temperature of [X] of water from 20℃ to 100℃? The parameter value for water volume is 1 L. If we already know the answer to the above question is 3.36×10^8 J, then what should [X] correspond to in the problem?

en: [ temperature increase of water]=[ final temperature]-[ initial temperature]
[ mass of water] = [ heat absorbed by water]/([ temperature increase of water]*[specific heat capacity of water])

question.en: A refrigerator works intermittently. The nameplate of a certain refrigerator shows the following parameters. question.en: Ningning uses an electric kettle to boil water, knowing that the kettle contains water with a mass of [X] and an initial temperature of 20°C. question.en: With the continuous improvement of the living standards of our people, automobiles have become essential tools for travel for many families. A certain brand of domestic car travels at a constant speed of 25m/s on a straight road [X], consuming 1.2kg of gasoline. Assuming the gasoline is completely burned in the engine cylinders, find during the process of the car traveling at a constant speed [X]: The work done by the car engine's traction force; the initial temperature parameter value is 20 ℃. If we already know that the answer to the above question is 3×10^7 J, then what should [X] correspond to in the problem?

question.en:
When heating water with a stove, [X] amount of water is heated from 20°C to 100°C, and 0.5 kg of coke is burned. The specific heat capacity of water is 4.2×10^3 J/(kg•°C), and the calorific value of coke is 3.0×10^7 J/kg. Calculate:
What is the efficiency of the stove when heating the water? The value of the parameter time is 1000 s. If we already know that the answer to the above question is 22.4%, then what should the content corresponding to [X] be in the question?

en: [ change in temperature of water]=[ final temperature]-[ initial temperature]
[ heat released by coke combustion]=[ mass of coke]×[ calorific value of coke]
[ heat absorbed by water] = [ efficiency of the stove heating water]*[ heat released by coke combustion]
[ mass of water] = [ heat absorbed by water]/([specific heat capacity of water]*[ change in temperature of water])

question.en: Xiao Ming's family recently purchased a new natural gas water heater. After learning about thermal efficiency, Xiao Ming attempted to estimate the thermal efficiency of the heater. If we already know the answer to the above problem is 4.2×10^6 J, what should the value corresponding to [X] be in the problem?

en: [ Volume of consumed gas] = [ Heat released by gas combustion]/[ Calorific value of the gas]

The illustration shows a diagram of drought-resistant water pumping in a certain village, with a pump flow rate of 180 m^3/h (the volume of water flowing out of the pipe per hour) and a pumping height H of [X] meters. (ρ_{diesel}=0.8×10^3kg/m^3, q_{diesel}=4.0×10^{7}J/kg, g is taken as 10 N/kg) Calculate:

What is the power of the useful work done by this mechanical device? The density of water is 1.0×10^3kg/m³ and the specific heat capacity of water is 4.2×10^3 J/(kg·℃). If we already know that the answer to the above question is 6000 W, what should [X] correspond to in the question?

en: [ water mass per hour]=[Water density]×[ water volume per hour]
[ gravitational force per hour]=[ water mass per hour]×[ gravitational acceleration]
[ useful work per hour] = [ power]*[ time]
[ pumping height] = [ useful work per hour]/[ gravitational force per hour]

question.en:
The diagram shows a prototype of an autonomous vehicle. When driving autonomously, the car uses radar sensors and laser rangefinders to understand the surrounding traffic conditions. The car travels at a constant speed of 20 m/s on a straight road for 3 km, consuming 0.4 kg of gasoline. Assuming the gasoline is completely burned and the calorific value of the gasoline is 4.5×10^7 J/kg, and the efficiency of the gasoline engine is [X], determine:

What is the resistance encountered by the car during travel? The final temperature of the water is 70 ℃. Given that the answer to the problem above is 1800 N, what should be the value of [X] in the problem?

en: [ heat generated by gasoline combustion]=[mass of gasoline consumed]×[ calorific value of gasoline]
[ traction force] = [ resistance]
[ energy converted to mechanical energy] = [ traction force]*[ driving distance]
[ efficiency of gasoline engine] = [ energy converted to mechanical energy]/[ heat generated by gasoline combustion]

question.en:
A certain type of "220V, 2000W" instant hot water and drinking integrated direct drinking machine can heat [X] water from 20°C to 90°C within 1 hour. (c_water=4.2×10^3J/(kg•°C), q_gas=3×10^7J/m^3)

Find:
What is the heating efficiency of the direct drinking machine? (Keep 1 decimal place) The calorific value of the fuel oil parameter is 4.0×10^7 J/kg. If we already know that the answer to the above question is 81.7%, then what should [X] be in the question?

en: [ temperature change of water]=[ final temperature]-[ initial temperature]
[ electric energy]=[ electric power]×[ time]
[ heat absorbed by water] = [ heating efficiency]*[ electric energy]
[ mass of water] = [ heat absorbed by water]/([specific heat capacity of water]*[ temperature change of water])

question.en: With the use of advanced technology and scientific methods, waste can be turned into treasure. If [X] kg of fuel oil can be extracted from 1 ton of waste, and the fuel oil has a calorific value of 4.5×10^7 J/kg, what is the amount of heat released when this fuel oil is completely burned? The time parameter value is 1 h. If we already know that the answer to the above question is 6.3×10^9 J, then what should be the content corresponding to [X] in the problem?

en: [mass of fuel oil] = [ heat released by complete combustion of fuel]/[ calorific value of fuel oil]

question.en: The gas renovation project of "doing practical things for the people" by the Guilin municipal government is rapidly advancing in the old city area. question.en:
The thermal efficiency of a gas water heater indicates what proportion of the chemical energy consumed when the gas is completely burned is converted into the internal energy of the water. A certain model of camper travels at a constant speed on a straight and level road for [X], taking 30 minutes. The total mass of the vehicle is 4×10^3 kg, and the resistance encountered is 1/8 of the vehicle's weight (assuming complete combustion of fuel, with fuel density ρ=0.8×10^3 kg/m^3, and fuel calorific value q is 4.5×10^7 J/kg, g is taken as 10 N/kg). Find:  

Knowing that fuel is consumed during this process, what is the efficiency of the camper's engine? (Supplementary: the traction force is 5×10^3 N; the fuel volume is 2×10^-2 m^3; the specific heat capacity of water is 4.2×10^3 J/(kg·℃)). If we already know the answer to the above question is 27.8%, what should the content corresponding to [X] be?

en: [ fuel mass]=[ fuel density]×[ fuel volume]
[ heat released by complete combustion of fuel]=[ fuel calorific value]×[ fuel mass]
[ work done by traction force] = [ thermal efficiency]*[ heat released by complete combustion of fuel]
[ distance] = [ work done by traction force]/[traction force]

arguments.en_name: heat released by complete combustion of fuel

question.en: A metal rod with a mass of 1 kilogram is heated for a period of time, and its temperature rises from 25℃ to [X]. Find the heat absorbed by the metal rod, Q_abs. [c_metal = 0.39×10^3 J/(kg·℃)] The volume of natural gas is given as 0.04 m^3. If we already know that the answer to the above question is 3.9×10^3 J, then what should [X] correspond to in the problem?

en: [ change in temperature] = [ heat absorbed by the metal rod Q_abs]/([ mass]*[ specific heat capacity of the metal])
[final temperature] = [ initial temperature] + [ change in temperature]

arguments.en_name: specific heat capacity of the metal
heat absorbed by the metal rod Q_abs

question.en:
A certain brand of multi-level health-preserving electric kettle has some parameters as shown in the table below. Based on the information in the table, solve the following problem:

| Rated Voltage | High Temperature Power | Low Temperature Power | Maximum Capacity |
|---------------|------------------------|-----------------------|------------------|
| 220V          | 2200W                  | [X]                   | 2L              |

During one use, the high temperature setting works for a total of 3 minutes, and the low temperature setting works for a total of 10 minutes. How much electrical energy is consumed in this use? The specific heat capacity of water is 4.2×10^3 J/(kg·℃). If we already know the answer to the above problem is 5.16×10^5 J, what should the content corresponding to [X] be?

en: [ Electrical energy consumed at high power setting]=[High power setting]×[ High power setting operation time]
[ Electrical energy consumed at low power setting] = [ Total electrical energy] - [ Electrical energy consumed at high power setting]
[ Low power setting] = [ Electrical energy consumed at low power setting]/[ Low power setting operation time]

arguments.en_name: Electrical energy consumed at high power setting
Electrical energy consumed at low power setting

question.en:
Under standard atmospheric pressure, a gas stove heats a kettle with a mass of [X] and a temperature of 20°C to boiling, taking approximately 10 minutes. The specific heat capacity of water is 4.2×10^3 J/(kg•°C), and the calorific value of natural gas is 4.2×10^7 J/m^3. Find: 

If 60% of the heat released by the complete combustion of natural gas is absorbed by the water, how much natural gas is needed to boil the kettle of water? (Supplementary: the boiling point is 100°C; the value of the parameter travel time is 1 hour.) If we already know that the answer to the above question is 0.04 m^3, what should the content corresponding to [X] be in the problem?

en: [ temperature increase of water]=[ boiling point]-[ initial temperature]
[ heat released by complete combustion of natural gas] = [ calorific value of natural gas]*[ volume of natural gas needed]
[ heat absorbed by water] = [ heat released by complete combustion of natural gas]*[ thermal efficiency]
[ mass of water] = [ heat absorbed by water]/([ temperature increase of water]*[specific heat capacity of water])

arguments.en_name: heat released by complete combustion of natural gas

question.en: When the domestic airplane "Y-20" flies at high altitude, under constant horizontal thrust, it cruises uniformly for 10 minutes along the horizontal direction, burning 80 kg of aviation fuel. Given that the useful work output of the airplane engine is [X], the heat value of aviation fuel is q=4.0×10^7 J/kg. Find: What is the useful power of the engine in watts? The heat value of the fuel is 4.6×10^7 J/kg. If we already know that the answer to the above question is 3.2×10^6 W, what should the content corresponding to [X] in the question be?

en: [useful work output of the engine] = [ useful power of the engine]*[ time]

arguments.en_name: useful work output of the engine

en: [ temperature increase of water]=[ boiling point]-[ initial temperature]
[mass of water] = [ heat absorbed by water]/([ temperature increase of water]*[ specific heat capacity of water])

question.en: A light truck with a mass of 3 tons and a rated power of 100 kW is loaded with 6 tons of sand and gravel. question.en: A mass of 1 kilogram of water has a temperature increase of [X]. Find the heat absorbed by the water, Q_abs. [c_water = 4.2×10^3 J/(kg•°C)] The value of the parameter time is 300 s. question.en:
Recently, many shared electric cars have appeared in our city. This new type of low-carbon transportation tool is very popular among citizens. Some parameters of a brand's electric car are shown in the table. Please answer:

| Battery Capacity (kW·h) | 22 |
| Onboard Charger Input Voltage (V) | 220 |
| Onboard Charger Input Current (A) | 16 |
| Efficiency of Converting Electrical Energy to Mechanical Energy | [X] |

According to the data in the table, how much time is theoretically needed to fully charge an already depleted battery? After being fully charged, the car's maximum distance traveled on a level surface at a constant speed is 140 kilometers. What is the resistance force experienced by the car during this movement? The specific heat capacity of iron is 0.45×10^3 J/(kg·°C). If we already know the answer to the above question is 396 N, then what should [X] correspond to in the problem?

en: [ electrical energy converted to mechanical energy] = [ resistance experienced by the vehicle during travel]*[ travel distance]
[ efficiency of converting electrical energy to mechanical energy] = [ electrical energy converted to mechanical energy]/[Battery capacity]

question.en:
A certain single-cylinder four-stroke internal combustion engine has a flywheel speed of 300 r/min, a piston area of 120 cm^2, and a piston stroke L of 0.3 m. If the average pressure of gas during the power stroke is [X], what is the power of this internal combustion engine in watts?
 (Supplement: The number of power strokes per minute is 150; ) The temperature rise of the water is 40 ℃. If we already know that the answer to the above question is 4500 W, what should be the content corresponding to [X] in the problem?

en: [ total work done per minute] = [ power]*[ time]
[ single work done] = [ total work done per minute]/[ work done frequency per minute]
[ average pressure of the gas on the piston] = [ single work done]/[ piston stroke]
[Average pressure of the gas] = [ average pressure of the gas on the piston]/[ piston area]

arguments.en_name: average pressure of the gas on the piston

question.en:
The continuous rainy weather has made it difficult to dry clothes at home. In order to dry clothes faster, Xuanxuan's mother bought a new clothes dryer. The dryer can dry up to 10 pieces of clothing at one time, and the nameplate is shown in the table below. One time, Xuanxuan turned off other electrical appliances at home, put 10 freshly washed wet clothes into the dryer, and after 11 minutes of power, Xuanxuan found that the clothes were just dry, with a total mass just reduced by [X], and observed that the electricity meter marked with 3000 rev/(kW•h) turned 500 rev during this period.
Model 2010A
Rated Voltage 220V
Rated Power 1000W
Net Weight 2.2kg
Timer 30—180min
Scientific research shows that 1g of water needs to absorb 2260J of heat to vaporize into water vapor at the same temperature. What is the amount of heat absorbed by clothes during this drying process? The value of the temperature rise of the water is 50 ℃. If we already know that the answer to the above question is 4.52×10^5 J, then what should the value corresponding to [X] in the question be?

en: [mass of water] = [ heat absorbed by clothing]/[ heat required to vaporize each gram of water]

arguments.en_name: heat required to vaporize each gram of water

question.en:
Complete combustion of 0.07 kg of coke releases heat, of which 60% is absorbed by 5 kg of water, under standard atmospheric pressure. Given c_water = 4.2×10^3 J/(kg•℃), q_coke = 3.0×10^7 J/kg, find:
If the initial temperature of the water is [X], after absorbing this heat, to what temperature does the water rise? The parameters for blower working time are set to 1 h. If we already know the answer to the above question is 80 ℃, what should the content corresponding to [X] be?

en: [ heat released from complete combustion of coke]=[mass of coke]×[ calorific value of coke]
[ heat absorbed by water]=[ efficiency]×[ heat released from complete combustion of coke]
[ temperature rise of water]=[ heat absorbed by water]/([ specific heat capacity of water]×[ mass of water])
[ initial temperature of water] = -[ temperature rise of water] + [ final temperature of water]

arguments.en_name: heat released from complete combustion of coke

question.en:
A driver drives a car that can run on both hydrogen and gasoline along a straight road at a constant speed of 72 km/h from point A to point B. The distance between A and B is 252 km, and the mass of gasoline in the tank at departure is [X]. Assuming both fuels burn completely in the cylinder and the traction force on the car remains constant at 1000 N, the entire journey consists of two stages as described (the calorific value of hydrogen, q_{hydrogen} = 1.44×10^8 J/kg, and the calorific value of gasoline, q_{gasoline} = 4.5×10^7 J/kg). Stage One: The car uses hydrogen as fuel to travel from A for 1 hour to reach point C. In Stage Two: Due to insufficient hydrogen, the driver switches to gasoline as fuel from C to B, with the gasoline just used up upon arrival at B. Find:
The efficiency of the car's engine in Stage Two. The parameter for the contact area per wheel with the ground is 0.05 m^2. If the answer to the above problem is known to be 40%, then what should [X] represent in the problem?

en: [ Stage Two Distance]=[Total Distance]-[ Stage One Distance]
[ Work Done by Traction Force in Stage Two]=[ Traction Force]×[ Stage Two Distance]
[ Heat Released by Complete Combustion of Gasoline] = [ Work Done by Traction Force in Stage Two]/[ Efficiency of the Car Engine in Stage Two]
[ Mass of Gasoline] = [ Heat Released by Complete Combustion of Gasoline]/[ Calorific Value of Gasoline]

arguments.en_name: Work Done by Traction Force in Stage Two
Heat Released by Complete Combustion of Gasoline
Efficiency of the Car Engine in Stage Two

Ignoring heat loss, how much can these heat raise the temperature of water with a mass of [X] from 60℃ in a standard atmospheric pressure? The specific heat capacity of water is 4.2×10^3 J/(kg·℃). The voltage of parameter 3 is 220 kV. If we already know that the answer to the above question is 50 ℃, what should correspond to [X] in the problem?

en: [ heat absorbed by water]=[ volume of natural gas]×[ calorific value of natural gas]
[ mass of water] = [ heat absorbed by water]/([ temperature increase of water]*[specific heat capacity of water])

question.en: "Garbage classification and green environmental protection": Proper classification and utilization of waste can turn waste into treasure. At a certain waste treatment plant, under certain conditions, 1t of classified waste can extract [X] fuel oil. The calorific value of this fuel oil is q=4.0×10^7J/kg, c_water=4.2×10^3J/(kg·℃). Please calculate: If 35% of this heat is absorbed by 10t of water, how many degrees Celsius can the water's temperature increase? The parameter of the rated voltage is 220 V. If we already know the answer to the above question is 40 ℃, then what should the content corresponding to [X] be in the problem?

en: [ heat absorbed by water] = [ rise in temperature of water]*[ specific heat capacity of water]*[ mass of water]
[ heat released by complete combustion of fuel oil] = 2.85714285714286*[ heat absorbed by water]
[mass of fuel oil] = [ heat released by complete combustion of fuel oil]/[ calorific value of fuel oil]

arguments.en_name: heat released by complete combustion of fuel oil

question.en:
Xiao Ming's mom uses hot water with a mass of [X] and an initial temperature of 95℃ to heat the milk. The milk has a mass of 420g and an initial temperature of 25℃. After heating for a period, their common temperature is 75℃. Given that the specific heat capacity of water is 4.2×10^3 J/(kg⋅℃), and assuming all heat released by the water is absorbed by the milk, find:
The specific heat capacity of the milk. The milk's temperature change is 50℃; the heat value of gasoline is 5×10^7 J/kg. If we already know that the answer to the above question is 2.5×10^3 J/(kg⋅℃), then what should the content corresponding to [X] be?

en: [ change in temperature of milk]=[ final temperature]-[ initial temperature]
[ heat absorbed by milk] = [ specific heat capacity of milk]*[ change in temperature of milk]*[ mass of milk]
[ heat released by hot water] = [ heat absorbed by milk]
[ mass of water] = [ heat released by hot water]/([specific heat capacity of water]*[ change in temperature of water])

question.en:
When boiling water on a gas stove, [X] cubic meters of natural gas are burned, raising the temperature of 100 kg of water from 20°C to 70°C. Given that the specific heat capacity of water is c=4.2×10^3 J/(kg•°C), and the calorific value of natural gas is q=7.0×10^7 J/m^3, find:  
1. The heat released by the complete combustion of [X] cubic meters of natural gas, Q_released.  
2. The initial temperature value is 20°C. If we already know that the answer to the above problem is 3.5×10^7 J, what should [X] be in the problem?

en: [volume] = [ heat released by complete combustion of natural gas]/[ calorific value]

arguments.en_name: heat released by complete combustion of natural gas

question.en: A driver drives a car that can operate on both hydrogen and gasoline along a straight highway at a constant speed of 72 km/h from location A to location B. The distance between location A and B is 252 km, and the gasoline mass in the tank at departure is 10 kg. Assume that both fuels are completely combusted in the cylinder, and the traction force experienced by the car during the journey is a constant 1000 N. The entire journey is divided into two stages as shown (Heat value of hydrogen q_{hydrogen} = 1.44×10^8 J/kg, heat value of gasoline q_{gasoline} = 4.5×10^7 J/kg). Stage one: The car uses hydrogen as fuel and departs from location A, travels for 1 hour, reaching location C, while using hydrogen. Stage two: Starting from location C, due to insufficient hydrogen, the driver switches to gasoline as fuel, and reaches location B with the gasoline in the tank completely used up. Find: the mass of hydrogen consumed by the car in stage one. (Supplement: the thermal efficiency is [X];) the final temperature parameter value is 70 °C. If we already know that the answer to the above question is 1 kg, then what should the content corresponding to [X] be?

en: [ distance traveled in phase one]=[velocity]×[ time]
[ work done by the car in phase one]=[ traction force]×[ distance traveled in phase one]
[ heat released by complete combustion of hydrogen] = [ calorific value of hydrogen]*[ mass of hydrogen consumed in phase one]
[ thermal efficiency] = [ work done by the car in phase one]/[ heat released by complete combustion of hydrogen]

arguments.en_name: work done by the car in phase one
heat released by complete combustion of hydrogen
mass of hydrogen consumed in phase one

question.en: An air fryer is a new kitchen appliance. The nameplate of the air fryer indicates: "220V [X]". If we already know that the answer to the above question is 0.55 kW·h, what should the content corresponding to [X] be in the question?

en: [rated power] = [ consumed electric energy]/[ operating time]

question.en:
A gas with a volume of 0.28 m^3 and a calorific value of 3.6×10^7 J/m^3 is completely burned. If 50% of the released heat is absorbed by water at a temperature of 20℃ and a mass of [X], what is the final temperature of the water? [The specific heat capacity of water is 4.2×10^3 J/(kg∙℃)]
The value of the working time parameter is 20 h. If we know the answer to the above question is 60 ℃, what should be the content corresponding to [X] in the problem?

en: [ heat released by complete combustion of gas]=[gas volume]×[ calorific value of gas]
[ heat absorbed by water]=[ efficiency]×[ heat released by complete combustion of gas]
[ temperature increase of water] = -[ initial temperature] + [ final temperature of water]
[ mass of water] = [ heat absorbed by water]/([ temperature increase of water]*[ specific heat capacity of water])

arguments.en_name: heat released by complete combustion of gas

question.en:
As shown, Chongqing's popular "wooden bucket fish" is made by placing high-temperature pebbles into a wooden bucket, then adding 2kg of fish soup with an initial temperature of 60°C. The heat released by the pebbles can make the fish soup boil at one standard atmosphere, with the specific heat capacity of the fish soup being the same as water's, c_water = 4.2×10^3J/(kg•°C). Find:

If 80% of the heat released by the pebbles is absorbed by the fish soup, what is the total heat released by the pebbles in J? (Supplement: the boiling point is [X];) The value of the time parameter is 2 hours. If we already know the answer to the above problem is 4.2×10^5J, then what should the content corresponding to [X] in the question be?

en: [ heat absorbed by fish soup] = 8000*[ heat released by cobblestones]
[ temperature increase of fish soup] = [ heat absorbed by fish soup]/([specific heat of water]*[ mass of fish soup])
[ boiling point] = [ initial temperature] + [ temperature increase of fish soup]

question.en: Energy is an important material basis for the progress and development of human society. Solar energy can be utilized everywhere, and it is clean and non-polluting, making it an ideal energy source. A solar water heater contains 50L of water, and under sunlight, the temperature of the water increases by [X]. (c_water = 4.2×10^3 J/(kg•℃), q_coke = 3.0×10^7 J/kg, ρ_water = 1.0×10^3 kg/m^3) Question: How many kilograms of coke would need to be completely burned to release the equivalent amount of heat? The value of the time parameter is 100 s. If we have already determined that the answer to this question is 0.21 kg, what should the content corresponding to [X] be in the question?

en: [ water mass]=[water density]×[ water volume]
[ heat released by coke] = [ calorific value of coke]*[ mass of coke]
[ heat absorbed by water] = [ heat released by coke]
[ temperature rise of water] = [ heat absorbed by water]/([ specific heat capacity of water]*[ water mass])

Hot water tank capacity[X]Heating power500W

en: [ temperature difference water increased]=[ final temperature]-[ initial temperature]
[ mass of water] = [ heat absorbed by water]/([ temperature difference water increased]*[ specific heat capacity of water])

question.en: Agricultural drones play an important role in modern agriculture due to their advantages of easy control, uniform spraying, and time efficiency. A certain model of agricultural drone with dual landing gear has the following parameters (density of pesticide ρ = 1.1×10^3 kg/m^3): ProjectParameterDimensions (length width height)3090mm*3090mm*680mmDrone mass[X]Tank capacity30LLanding gear base area (single)1×10^{-2}m^2Polymer power battery30000mA·hCharging voltage40VOptimal operating speed8m/s Find the pressure of the drone on the horizontal ground when it is stationary and unloaded (g = 10N/kg); given that the value of the natural gas heat value is 3.6×10^7 J/m^3. If we already know that the answer to the above problem is 1×10^4 Pa, then what should be the content corresponding to [X] in the question?

en: [ contact area]=2×[ single landing gear base area]
[ force] = [ pressure]*[ contact area]
[ drone weight] = [ force]
[mass] = [ drone weight]/[ gravitational acceleration]

question.en:

Reasonably classified waste can be utilized to turn waste into treasure; if 1 ton of waste can extract 0.21 tons of fuel oil, and the calorific value of the fuel oil is 4.0×10^7J/kg, with the specific heat capacity of water c_water=4.2×10^3J/(kg·℃). How should this resistor be connected in the circuit? What should be the resistance value of this resistor? The temperature parameter is 60 ℃. If we already know that the answer to the above question is 12 Ω, what should be the value of [X] in the problem?

en: [ the voltage across the series resistor]=[ the voltage of the power supply]﹣[The voltage across the light bulb]
[ the current when the light bulb is lit normally] = [ the voltage across the series resistor]/[ the series resistor]
[ the resistance of the light bulb] = [The voltage across the light bulb]/[ the current when the light bulb is lit normally]

arguments.en_name: The voltage across the light bulb
the resistance of the light bulb
the current when the light bulb is lit normally
the voltage of the power supply
the voltage across the series resistor

question.en:
A mass of m=1kg slides down from a slope and reaches point A at the bottom with a velocity of v=[X]. It then moves 1m on a horizontal surface and stops at point B. It is known that the expression for the kinetic energy of the object is E_k=1/2mv^2, with the unit of Joules (J), and 50% of the kinetic energy decrease from point A to B is used to increase the object's temperature. The specific heat capacity of the object is c=0.4×10^3 J/(kg•°C). Calculate:

The kinetic energy of the object at point A; the temperature change of water is 40 ℃. If we already know that the answer to the above question is 2 J, what should the content corresponding to [X] be?

en: [ velocity] = -1.4142135623731*sqrt([ kinetic energy of the object at point A]/[mass])

arguments.en_name: kinetic energy of the object at point A

question.en: The "Yun-20" is a large transport aircraft independently developed by our country. Its engine is a heat engine, which generates thrust by burning aviation kerosene in the combustion chamber and expelling gases at high speed from the nozzle, propelling the engine forward. If the "Yun-20" flies at a high altitude with a constant horizontal thrust [X] and travels 360 km horizontally at a constant speed in 0.5 hours, consuming 2250 kg of aviation kerosene, given that the calorific value of aviation kerosene is q = 4.0×10^7 J/kg. In this flight, find: the thermal efficiency of the transport aircraft's engine. If we already know that the above question's answer is 60%, then what should the content corresponding to [X] in the question be?

en: [ heat released by complete combustion of fuel]=[ fuel mass]×[ calorific value]
[ work done by thrust] = [ thermal efficiency]*[ heat released by complete combustion of fuel]
[thrust] = [ work done by thrust]/[ distance]

arguments.en_name: heat released by complete combustion of fuel

question.en: Xiao Cong purchased a "Solar Sail" brand solar water heater, and he noticed the parameters of this water heater as follows: Vacuum tube diameter × length (mm)70×1800Specifications (branch pipe)15Overall dimensions (mm)1840×1597×1765Insulation layer (mm)60Water tank capacity (L)120Lighting area (m^2)2.0 Assuming that the sunlight intensity is 3×10^6J/(m^2•h) (the sunlight intensity represents the energy of sunlight received per square meter area in 1h). If the daily time for receiving solar energy is calculated as [X], and the heater can convert 50% of the received solar energy into the internal energy of water. Question: Under normal sunlight, how many degrees Celsius can the temperature of a full tank of water initially at 20°C be raised within a day by this water heater? (The specific heat capacity of water is c=4.2×10^3J/(kg•°C)). If we already know that the answer to the above question is 50°C, what should the content corresponding to [X] be?

en: [ heat absorbed by water] = [ temperature increase of water]*[ specific heat capacity of water]*[ mass of water]
[ received solar energy] = [ heat absorbed by water]/[ efficiency]
[ illumination time] = [ received solar energy]/([Sunlight intensity]*[ lighting area])

question.en:
An electric water heater marked "220V800W" is filled with 0.5kg of water. After operating normally for a period of time, the water is heated from [X] to 100°C. Given that c_water = 4.2×10^3 J/(kg•°C), ignoring heat loss. Calculate:
The heat absorbed by the water; the value of the consumed gas volume is 0.25 m^3. If we already know that the answer to the above problem is 1.68×10^5 J, then what should be the value corresponding to [X] in the problem?

en: [ temperature increase of water] = [ heat absorbed by water]/([specific heat capacity of water]*[ mass of water])
[ initial temperature] = [ final temperature] - [ temperature increase of water]

question.en:
Figure 1 shows a ship entirely powered by solar energy. The ship is 30 meters long, 15 meters wide, with a displacement of 60 tons. Solar panels are mounted on the ship's surface, receiving solar energy at a power of 1.6×10^5W, solely used to propel the ship forward. During a voyage, starting from a certain moment, the horizontal traction force F exerted on the solar-powered ship changes over time as shown in Figure 2a, and the ship's velocity v changes over time as shown in Figure 2b. (g is taken as 10 N/kg)

Calculate:

The work done by the traction force from the 50th second to the 100th second; during the period from the 50th second to the 100th second, the ship's speed is [X] and during this period, the traction force is 8×10^4N. The calorific value of the fuel is 5.0×10^7 J/kg. If we already know the answer to the above question is 2×10^6 J, what should be substituted for [X] in the problem statement?

en: [ travel distance] = [ work done by traction force]/[ traction force]
[Ship speed] = [ travel distance]/[ time]

question.en:
The "Red Flag HQ3" autonomous vehicle, independently developed in China, is undergoing testing on a straight road. The car travels at a constant speed of 18 m/s for 5 minutes, consuming 0.3 kg of fuel, and the engine's traction force is [X]. Given that the fuel's heating value is 4.5×10^7 J/kg, find:  
What is the work done by the car's traction force? (Additional information: the travel distance is 5400 m; ) The initial temperature parameter is 20 ℃. If we know the answer to the above question is 5.4×10^6 J, what should the content corresponding to [X] be in the problem?

en: [ traction force] = [ work done by the car's traction force]/[travel distance]

arguments.en_name: work done by the car's traction force

question.en:
Xiao Hua's family uses a natural gas water heater, and he tries to estimate the efficiency of the heater to check if the value on the nameplate is accurate. When the water heater is the only device using natural gas, it heats 50 kg of water from 20°C to 54°C, and the natural gas meter reading changes from 1365.05 m^3 to [X]. Given the specific heat capacity of water c = 4.2×10^3 J/(kg·°C), and the calorific value of natural gas q = 7.0×10^7 J/m^3, find:
The heat released by the complete combustion of the consumed natural gas; the mass of the water is 50 kg. If we already know the answer to the above question is 8.4×10^6 J, what should the value of [X] be in the problem?

en: [ Consumed natural gas volume] = [ Heat released from complete combustion of natural gas]/[ Calorific value of natural gas]
[Final state volume] = [ Initial state volume] + [ Consumed natural gas volume]

arguments.en_name: Heat released from complete combustion of natural gas

A model of teapot Model: JY﹣﹣﹣456
Rated voltage: 220V Frequency: 50Hz

question.en: There is a portable garment steamer used for ironing clothes. After being powered on, the water in the tank with volume [X] is heated from 20℃ to 100℃. question.en: The bulb L_1 is marked with "[X], 3W", the maximum resistance of the variable resistor R is 30Ω, the power supply voltage and the bulb resistance remain unchanged, and the ammeter range is 0-0.6A. question.en: As shown in the table, this is the nameplate of the household electric water heater, where the resistance values of heating elements R_1 and R_2 remain unchanged. question.en:

question.en:

question.en: During the melting process, a crystal absorbs heat. In physics, the ratio of the heat absorbed by 0°C ice as it completely melts into 0°C water to its mass is called the latent heat of ice, represented by the letter λ. Now, when heating [X] of ice with an initial temperature of -20°C using an alcohol burner with an efficiency of 35%, a total of 16g of alcohol is burned as the ice starts melting until it is completely melted into 0°C water. Given that the specific heat capacity of ice is c_ice=2.1×10^3 J/(kg·°C) and the calorific value of alcohol is 3×10^7 J/kg, find: What is the latent heat of ice λ_ice? The value of the parameter input voltage is 220 V. If we already know that the answer to the above question is 3.36×10^5 J/kg, then what should the content corresponding to [X] in the problem be?

en: [ Heat released by alcohol combustion]=[Mass of alcohol]×[ Calorific value of alcohol]
[ Heat absorbed by melting ice]=[ Thermal efficiency]×[ Heat released by alcohol combustion]
[ Mass of ice] = [ Heat absorbed by melting ice]/[ Heat of fusion of ice water]

arguments.en_name: Heat of fusion of ice water

question.en: During the Beijing Winter Olympics, multiple hydrogen fuel buses were put into operation. Hydrogen fuel is considered the ideal energy of the 21st century due to its cleanliness and high efficiency. Given c_water=4.2×10^3J/(kg·℃) and q_hydrogen=1.4×10^8J/kg, calculate the temperature increase of water if 80% of this energy is absorbed entirely by 800 kg of water initially at 10℃ under standard atmospheric pressure. (Supplement: The heat released by hydrogen fuel is [X];) the duration for the parameter value is 10 minutes. If we already know that the answer to the above question is 70℃, what should the content corresponding to [X] in the problem be?

en: [ heat absorbed by water] = [ temperature rise of water]*[specific heat capacity of water]*[ mass of water]
[ heat released by hydrogen fuel] = [ heat absorbed by water]/[ efficiency]

question.en: A school has a total of 400 "220V40W" fluorescent lamps, with an average daily electricity consumption of [X]. To improve lighting and save electricity, they are now all replaced with "220V11W" energy-saving lamps. Find: the amount of electrical energy the school can save in one day. The calorific value of natural gas is 3.2×10^7 J/m^3. If we already know that the answer to the above question is 58 kW·h, what should [X] correspond to in the problem?

en: [ daily usage time] = [ daily energy savings of the school]/(400*([power of each fluorescent lamp] - [ power of each energy-saving lamp]))

arguments.en_name: energy consumption of 400 fluorescent lamps per day
energy consumption of 400 energy-saving lamps per day
daily energy savings of the school

question.en: A new type of fighter jet independently developed by our country possesses excellent performance such as supersonic cruise, electromagnetic stealth, and beyond-visual-range attack. The maximum takeoff weight of the aircraft is 37t, the maximum flight altitude reaches 20000m, the maximum cruise speed is 2.5 times the speed of sound (equivalent to 3060km/h), and the maximum fuel load is 10t. The relationship between the drag force experienced by the aircraft during flight and speed is shown in the table below: Speed v (m/s) 100 200 300 400 500 Drag force f/N 0.3×10^4 1.2×10^4 2.7×10^4 4.8×10^4 7.5×10^4 The aviation fuel used by the aircraft has a calorific value of 5×10^7J/kg. If the fuel tank is filled, and the aircraft cruises at a speed of 500m/s, with a maximum range of approximately 2.6×10^3km, what is the approximate efficiency of the aircraft's engine? (Supplement: The calorific value of the fuel is 5×10^7J/kg; the range is [X];) The initial temperature parameter is given as 24 ℃. If we already know the answer to the above question is 39%, what should the content corresponding to [X] be in the question?

en: [ heat generated by complete combustion of fuel]=[Fuel mass]×[ calorific value of fuel]
[ work done by engine] = [ engine efficiency]*[ heat generated by complete combustion of fuel]
[ range] = [ work done by engine]/[ resistance]

arguments.en_name: heat generated by complete combustion of fuel

question.en: With the progress of society, people's living standards are constantly improving, and refrigerators have become indispensable appliances in modern households. The following table is the nameplate of a certain brand of refrigerator in Xiao Ming's home. ModelABC66Rated Voltage[X]Rated Power110W The main working component of a refrigerator is the compressor (the compressor is actually a motor), and when the refrigerator is working normally, the compressor converts electrical energy into mechanical energy and thermal energy. If the resistance of the compressor coil is 8, what is the mechanical power of the compressor in watts when the refrigerator is working normally? The value of the parameter coal's mass is 0.2 kg. If we already know the answer to the above question is 108 W, what should the content corresponding to [X] in the problem be?

en: [ compressor heating power] = -[ mechanical power of the compressor] + [Rated power]
[ current] = -sqrt([ compressor heating power]/[ compressor coil resistance])
[ rated voltage] = [Rated power]/[ current]

question.en: On March 12, the "Tian Kun Hao" cutter suction dredger, independently developed and built by our country, officially commenced its first voyage. Its level of intelligence and high power configuration of excavation and conveying systems are among the best in the world. (Take g as 10 N/kg, and ρ_water as 1.0×10^3 kg/m^3). The main parameters are shown in the table below. Item Parameter Total length (m) 140 Width (m) 27.8 Diameter of suction/discharge pipes (mm) 1000/1000 Full-load displacement (t) 1.7×10^4 Full-load draft depth (m) 6.5 Mud pump delivery power (W) 1.7×10^7 When fully loaded, what is the pressure exerted by water on the bottom of "Tian Kun Hao"? If it is necessary to install a detection instrument on the bottom of the ship, and its area is [X], what is the pressure exerted by water on the detection instrument? The temperature at the end of the parameter is 55 °C. If we already know the answer to the above question is 260 N, then what should [X] correspond to in the problem?

en: [ water pressure at the bottom]=[Density of water]×[ acceleration due to gravity]×[ full load draft depth]
[ area of the detection instrument] = [ pressure on the detection instrument due to water]/[ water pressure at the bottom]

arguments.en_name: pressure on the detection instrument due to water
arguments.en_symbol: 探测仪器受到水的压力

question.en: At a standard atmospheric pressure, 50L of water is heated from 40°C to its boiling point. Find: the amount of heat the water needs to absorb. The density of water is 1.0×10³ kg/m³, the boiling point of water is [X], the specific heat capacity of water is 4.2×10³ J/(kg·°C), and the calorific value of gas is 4.2×10^7 J/m³. If we already know the answer to the above problem is 1.26×10^7 J, then what should the content corresponding to [X] be?

en: [ water mass]=[ water density]×[Water volume]
[ change in water temperature] = [ heat required by water to absorb]/([ specific heat capacity of water]*[ water mass])
[ boiling point temperature] = [ initial temperature] + [ change in water temperature]

arguments.en_name: heat required by water to absorb

question.en: The engine is the core component of a car, and the quality of the engine determines the performance and quality of the whole vehicle. For a car using 93-octane gasoline as fuel, the relevant data of its engine is shown in the table below. The air-fuel ratio in the table refers to the mass ratio of air to fuel in the cylinder. Number of working cycles completed in 1 minute2400Density of gasoline and air mixture in cylinder1.3 kg/m^3Working volume of cylinder1.8 LCalorific value of gasoline4.6×10^7 J/kgMaximum power of engine82.8 kWAir-fuel ratio12:1 When the car completes one working cycle, what is the mass of the gasoline and air mixture in the cylinder in kg, what is the mass of the gasoline in the cylinder in kg, and how much heat is released from the complete combustion of the fuel? The working volume of the cylinder is 1.8×10^(-3) m³; in one working cycle, the mass of gasoline in the cylinder is the value of the temperature rise of [X] parameter water by 50 ℃. If we already know the answer to the above question is 8.28×10^3 J, what should the content corresponding to [X] in the question be?

en: [gasoline mass] = [ total heat released by complete combustion of fuel]/[ gasoline calorific value]

arguments.en_name: total heat released by complete combustion of fuel

question.en:
Natural gas stoves are convenient, economical, and environmentally friendly. As shown, under standard atmospheric pressure, a natural gas stove heats a kettle with a mass of 3 kg and a temperature of 20°C to boiling in approximately 10 minutes. Given that the specific heat capacity of water is 4.2×10^3 J/(kg•°C) and the calorific value of natural gas is 3.5×10^7 J/m^3, find:
The amount of heat absorbed by the water; The boiling point temperature of the water is [X] parameter If the calorific value of natural gas is 3.6×10^7 J/m^3. If we already know that the answer to the above question is 1.008×10^6 J, what should be the content corresponding to [X] in the question?

en: [ temperature increase of water] = [ heat absorbed by water]/([specific heat capacity of water]*[ mass of water])
[ boiling point temperature] = [ initial temperature] + [ temperature increase of water]

question.en: Xiao Ming's family recently bought a new natural gas water heater with a capacity of 80L. After learning about thermal efficiency, Xiao Ming tried to estimate the thermal efficiency of this water heater. He set the "inflow" to 40L and the "outflow temperature" to 40℃ and started heating. The heating automatically stopped when the water temperature reached 40℃. It is known that the temperature of the tap water at the time was 20℃, the reading on the natural gas meter was 129.96m^3 before heating, and it became 130.06m^3 after heating stopped. The calorific value of natural gas, q_{natural gas} = 4.2×10^7J/m^3, the specific heat capacity of water, c_water = 4.2×10^3J/(kg•℃), and 1L=1.0^{﹣3}m^3. Find: the heat absorbed by the water in the tank, given that the density of water is 1.0×10^3kg/m^3 (Supplement: Volume is [X]; Volume of water is [X];) the value of normal operating voltage is 15 V. If we already know that the answer to the above question is 3.36×10^6 J, then what should be the content corresponding to [X] in the problem?

en: [ Mass of water]=[ Volume of water]×[Density of water]
[ Temperature change of water]=[ Final temperature]-[ Initial temperature]
[ Heat absorbed by water]=[ Specific heat capacity of water]×[ Mass of water]×[ Temperature change of water]
[ Volume] = [ Mass of water]/[Density of water]

question.en:
In the experiment "Investigating the characteristics of temperature change during water boiling," a spirit lamp is used to heat water in a beaker. The beaker contains water with an initial temperature of 20℃ and a mass of 0.1 kg, heated to boiling under standard atmospheric pressure, with the alcohol [X] completely burned. (Given that the specific heat capacity of water is 4.2×10^3 J/(kg·℃), the calorific value of alcohol is 3.0×10^7 J/kg) Find:  
The thermal efficiency of the spirit lamp during the process of boiling water. (Supplementary: the final temperature is 100℃; ) the average working current value of the parameters is 7 A. If we have already known that the answer to the above question is 37.33 %, then what should [X] correspond to in the question?

en: [ temperature change of water]=[ final temperature]-[ initial temperature]
[ heat absorbed by water]=[specific heat capacity of water]×[ mass of water]×[ temperature change of water]
[ heat released by complete combustion of alcohol] = [ heat absorbed by water]/[ thermal efficiency]
[ mass of alcohol] = [ heat released by complete combustion of alcohol]/[ calorific value of alcohol]

arguments.en_name: heat released by complete combustion of alcohol

question.en: As the living standards of people continue to rise, cars increasingly become a part of everyday households. A car using gasoline as fuel travels at a constant speed of 72 km/h on a horizontal road, with an actual engine power of 20 kW. If the car travels a distance of [X], with a gasoline calorific value q = 4.6×10^7 J/kg, and the car's engine efficiency is 25%, find the work done by the engine over this distance; a car traveling at 72 km/h for a distance of [X] reaches a final temperature of 70 ℃. If we already know the answer to the above problem is 1×10^8J, what should be the content corresponding to [X] in the problem?

en: [ time] = [ work done by the engine]/[ power]
[Travel distance] = [ time]*[ speed]

question.en:
A kettle contains [X] kg of water at 20°C, and it is heated to boiling using a natural gas stove. Given that the calorific value of natural gas is 8×10^7 J/m^3, the atmospheric pressure is 1 standard atmosphere, and the specific heat capacity of water is 4.2×10^3 J/(kg°C). Find:
If the natural gas consumed to boil this water results in a stove efficiency of 40%, what should [X] be if the volume of natural gas consumed is 0.021 m^3 and the final temperature is 100°C, with the given time being 10 minutes?

en: [ temperature change of water]=[ final temperature]-[ initial temperature]
[ heat released by natural gas]=[ calorific value of natural gas]×[ volume of natural gas consumed]
[ heat absorbed by water] = [ heat released by natural gas]*[ efficiency of gas stove]
[ mass of water] = [ heat absorbed by water]/([specific heat capacity of water]*[ temperature change of water])

question.en:
In a physics interest group, students use a coal stove to heat 50 kg of water with an initial temperature of 20℃, and at the same time, they plot a graph showing how the water temperature changes over time during the heating process. If 2 kg of coal is completely burned within 6 minutes, the specific heat capacity of water is 4.2×10^3 J/(kg⋅℃), and the calorific value of coal is approximately 3×10^7 J/kg. Find:
The amount of heat absorbed by the water after 6 minutes of heating; the final temperature of the water is [X], with the time parameter value being 600 s. If we already know the answer to the above question is 1.26×10^7 J, then what should be the content corresponding to [X] in the problem?

en: [ temperature rise of water] = [ heat absorbed by water]/([ specific heat capacity of water]*[mass of water])
[ final temperature] = [ initial temperature] + [ temperature rise of water]

question.en:
The image shows a commonly used electric kettle, with some technical parameters listed in the table below. Find:  
The electrical energy consumed by the electric kettle when it operates normally for 6 minutes.  
The rated power of the electric kettle is [X]. The mass of water is 5 kg. If we already know the answer to the question above is 3.96×10^5 J, then what should be the content corresponding to [X] in the question?

question.en:
A solar water heater is injected with [X] water. After being exposed to sunlight for some time, the water temperature rises from 10°C to 50°C. The specific heat capacity of water is 4.2×10^3 J/(kg·°C). 

Question: 

How much heat is absorbed by the water in this heater during this time? (Supplement: The temperature difference with the water temperature rise is 40°C; ) The heating value of gas is 4.2×10^7 J/kg. question.en: "Garbage classification, green and environmental protection." Reasonable classification and utilization of garbage can turn waste into treasure. A garbage disposal plant can extract 140 kg of fuel oil from 1t of classified garbage under certain conditions. If a community produces [X] of garbage per day, [the calorific value of the fuel oil is q=4.0×10^7J/kg, q_coal=3×10^7J/kg, c_water=4.2×10^3J/(kg•℃)]. Find: the amount of heat released when the fuel oil extracted from [X] of garbage is completely burned; the specific heat capacity of water is 4.2×10^3 J/(kg·℃). heat released by complete combustion of fuel oil

question.en: Energy-saving brand gas water heater, the nameplate indicates 10L/min, that is, after starting to heat, [X] of hot water is discharged every minute. If the initial temperature of the water entering the heater is 5℃, the temperature of the hot water flowing out is 45℃, and the efficiency of the water heater is 40%, given that the density of water is 1.0×10^3kg/m^3, the specific heat capacity of water is 4.2×10^3J/(kg⋅℃), and the calorific value of natural gas is 3.2×10^7J/m^3, find: the amount of heat released per minute when the natural gas is completely burned. The calorific value of ethanol is 3.0×10^7 J/kg. If we already know that the answer to the above question is 4.2×10^6 J, what should the content corresponding to [X] be in the question?

question.en:
The Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macao Bridge officially opened to traffic at 9:00 am on October 24, 2018. The total length of the bridge is 55 km, with approximately 40 km between the Zhuhai Port and the Hong Kong Port. The design speed is 100 km/h. A family car travels from the Zhuhai Port to the Hong Kong Port at the design speed and consumes gasoline [X]. The calorific value of gasoline is q=4.6×10^7 J/kg, and the resistance experienced by the car is constantly 1000 N. Find:
How much heat can be released if the gasoline consumed by the family car during this journey is completely burned? The final temperature parameter value is 80 ℃. If we already know the answer to the above question is 9.66×10^7 J, what should the content corresponding to [X] in the question be?

en: [Gasoline mass] = [ heat released from complete combustion of gasoline]/[ gasoline heating value]

arguments.en_name: heat released from complete combustion of gasoline

question.en: In order to ensure increased summer grain harvest and production this year, some counties and districts in our city have used plant protection drones to carry out "one spray three protection" operation on wheat. As shown: A certain brand of plant protection drone, with a total mass of 20 kg after being filled with pesticide and gasoline, has a bottom bracket with a contact area of 50 cm^2 with the horizontal ground. During a spraying operation, the drone sprays at a constant horizontal speed of [X] for 3 minutes, consuming 100 mL of gasoline. Given that the density of gasoline is 0.71×10^3 kg/m^3 with a calorific value of 4.6×10^7 J/kg, and g is taken as 10 N/kg, find the drone's horizontal travel distance in 3 minutes; the calorific value of natural gas is known to be 8.0×10^7 J/m³. If we already know that the above problem's answer is 900 m, then what should be the content corresponding to [X] in the question?

en: [ time]=[ spray duration]×60s/min
[speed] = [ horizontal distance]/[ time]

question.en:
Xiao Qing disconnects other electrical appliances at home from the power supply, leaving only the shower heater on, to measure the thermal efficiency of the electric shower heater using the electricity meter. He heats the water inside the shower heater, with a mass of 50 kg and an initial temperature of [X], to 55℃, and reads the electricity meter before and after heating. Find:

The heat absorbed by the water; the specific heat capacity of water is 4.2×10^3 J/(kg·℃). The current value when watching the video is 0.3 A. If we already know the answer to the above problem is 6.3×10^6 J, what should the content corresponding to [X] in the question be?

en: [ temperature change of water] = [ heat absorbed by water]/([ specific heat capacity of water]*[ mass of water])
[ initial temperature of water] = [final temperature of water] - [ temperature change of water]

question.en:
Over the forty years of reform and opening up, China's economy has developed rapidly, and the living standards of the people have significantly improved. Cars have become common household items. Xiaoming's car consumes 12.5L of gasoline for a 100km drive, taking 1.5 hours. Assuming the gasoline is completely burned, what is the actual output power of the engine [X]? Please complete the following question:
What is the work output by the car engine during the 100km journey? (Supplementary information: the power is [X];) The mass of the water parameter is 100 kg. If we already know the answer to the above question is 1.35×10^8 J, then what should be the content corresponding to [X] in the problem?

en: [Power] = [ engine output power]/[ time]

question.en:
A solar water heater is one of the devices that converts solar energy into internal energy. A certain brand of solar water heater receives an average of 4.2×10^6 J of solar energy per hour. During the 5 hours of effective exposure time, it raises the temperature of water in the heater, with a volume of [X] and an initial temperature of 20℃, to 40℃. Find:
The efficiency η of the water heater; the density of water is 1.0×10^3 kg/m³ (Supplementary: The specific heat capacity of water is 4.2×10³ J/(kg·℃);), and the calorific value of gas is 4.2×10^7 J/kg. question.en:
Natural gas is a clean fuel. Many taxis in Suzhou have already used natural gas instead of gasoline, and a certain taxi consumed [X] of natural gas over a period of time. Find:
If 30% of the heat is used for useful work, how far can a taxi travel at a constant speed with a traction force of 5×10^3 N? question.en: Rapeseed oil is a material commonly used in cooking, with the most suitable cooking temperature being 150～180℃. question.en: As shown in A, this is a domestically-produced negative pressure cabin ambulance with an unladen mass of 3.6t and a total tire-ground contact area of 1200cm^2. question.en:
A certain group of physics enthusiasts heated 10 kg of water using a coal stove. The graph shows how the temperature of the water changes over time during the heating process. If 2 kg of coal were completely burned within 6 minutes, the specific heat capacity of water is 4.2×10^3 J/(kg•℃), and the calorific value of coal is 3×10^7 J/kg. Find:

The efficiency of the coal stove in heating the water. The change in water temperature is [X] where the volume of shale gas is 1 m^3. If we already know that the answer to the above question is 4.2%, what should the content corresponding to [X] be?

en: [ heat released by complete combustion of coal]=[ mass of coal]×[ calorific value of coal]
[ heat absorbed by water] = [ heat released by complete combustion of coal]*[ thermal efficiency of coal stove when heating water]
[ change in temperature of water] = [ heat absorbed by water]/([ specific heat capacity of water]*[mass of water])

arguments.en_name: heat released by complete combustion of coal
thermal efficiency of coal stove when heating water

question.en: A certain middle school supplies students with hot water by heating 200 kg of water from 25℃ to 100℃ using a boiler. [X] kg of anthracite coal was burned. The calorific value of anthracite coal is 3.4×10^7J/kg. Find: What is the amount of heat released by the complete combustion of anthracite coal? The boiling point temperature parameter is 100℃. If we already know that the answer to the above question is 2.04×10^8 J, then what should be the content corresponding to [X] in the problem?

en: [mass of anthracite] = [ heat released by complete combustion of anthracite]/[ calorific value of anthracite]

arguments.en_name: heat released by complete combustion of anthracite

question.en:
The problem involves a grab crane powered by a diesel engine, with certain parameters listed in the table below. Calculate:
Unladen Mass [X]
Maximum Grab Height 6m
Maximum Driving Power While Unladen 4×10^4W
Diesel Engine Efficiency 40%
When the crane lifts 1.2t of timber and remains stationary on a horizontal surface, the pressure on the ground is 3×10^5Pa. What is the contact area with the ground? (g=10N/kg) The value of the power supply voltage is 220 V. If it is known that the answer to the above question is 0.2 m^2, then what should be the content corresponding to [X]?

en: [ force] = [ pressure]*[ contact area]
[ total gravity] = [ force]
[ total mass] = [ total gravity]/[ gravitational acceleration]
[Crane's empty mass] = [ total mass] - [ wood's mass]

question.en:
A farmhouse uses a stove to boil water, heating 20 kg of water from 20°C to 100°C, completely burning [X] of dry firewood. The specific heat capacity of water is 4.2×10^3 J/(kg·°C), and the calorific value of dry firewood is 1.2×10^7 J/kg. Find:
What is the heat released by the complete combustion of the dry firewood? The value of the contact area between the tire and the road surface is 750 cm². If we already know that the answer to the above question is 2.4×10^7 J, then what should [X] correspond to in the problem?

en: [Mass of dry firewood] = [ heat released by complete combustion of dry firewood]/[ calorific value of dry firewood]

arguments.en_name: heat released by complete combustion of dry firewood

question.en:
Using a gas stove to heat 2 kg of water from an initial temperature of 20℃ to [X] consumes 20 g of gas. Given that the specific heat capacity of water is 4.2×10^3 J/(kg•℃) and the calorific value of gas is 4.2×10^7 J/kg, determine:  
How much heat is absorbed by the water? The parameter value for time is 0.5 h. If we already know the answer to the above question is 4.2×10^5 J, then what should the content corresponding to [X] be?

en: [ temperature increase of water] = [ heat absorbed by water]/([specific heat capacity of water]*[ mass of water])
[ final temperature] = [ initial temperature] + [ temperature increase of water]

question.en: Using a gas stove to boil water, [X] kg of gas is burned to increase the temperature of 50 kg of water from 20℃ to 70℃. The specific heat capacity of water is known to be 4200 J/(kg•℃), and the calorific value of the gas is 4.2×10^7 J/kg. Find: the efficiency of the gas stove used to boil water. The voltage value of the parameter is 220 V. If we already know the answer to the above question is 50%, then what should the content corresponding to [X] be in the question?

en: [ heat absorbed by water]=[ mass of water]×[ specific heat capacity of water]×[ temperature difference of water heating]
[ heat released by complete combustion of gas] = [ heat absorbed by water]/[ efficiency of gas stove boiling water]
[mass of gas] = [ heat released by complete combustion of gas]/[ calorific value of gas]

arguments.en_name: heat released by complete combustion of gas
efficiency of gas stove boiling water

question.en:
On May 18th this year, China became the first in the world to achieve safe and controllable extraction of combustible ice. After decomposing 1m^3 of combustible ice, approximately [X] of natural gas is released. Given q_{natural gas}=2.1×10^7J/m^3, c_{water}=4.2×10^3J/(kg·℃). Calculate:
If all the heat is absorbed by water, how many kg of water can be heated from 20℃ to 95℃? The parameter time is given as 10 min. If we already know the answer to the above question is 10^4 kg, then what should the content corresponding to [X] in the question be?

en: [ temperature increase of water]=[ final temperature]-[ initial temperature]
[ heat absorbed by water] = [ temperature increase of water]*[ specific heat capacity of water]*[ mass of water]
[ heat released by natural gas] = [ heat absorbed by water]
[Volume of decomposed natural gas] = [ heat released by natural gas]/[ calorific value of natural gas]

question.en: With the continuous improvement of people's living standards, cars are increasingly becoming a part of everyday life. A car using gasoline as fuel, with a mass of 1.5 tons, travels at a speed of [X] on a horizontal road for 108 km at constant speed, consuming 9 kg of gasoline. The actual power of the engine is 23 kW. Given that the heat value of gasoline q = 4.6×10^7 J/kg, calculate the time taken for the car on this journey: (Supplement: the speed is [X];) the initial parameter temperature is 25 ℃. If we already know that the answer to the above question is 5.4×10^3 s, then what should the content corresponding to [X] be in the problem?

en: [ speed] = [distance]/[ travel time]

question.en: In this battle against the COVID-19 pandemic, traditional Chinese medicine has played an active role in diagnosis and treatment, becoming an important part of the "Chinese approach" to epidemic prevention. If we already know that the answer to the above problem is 88 Ω, what should be the content corresponding to [X] in the problem?

en: [ total resistance of high-temperature setting] = [ resistance value of a single heating resistor]/2

question.en:
